title: Semicontinuity and base change
statement:
Let $f:X\to T$ be a proper morphism of finite presentation and $\cF$ an
$\cO_X$-module of finite presentation, flat over $T$. For every integer
$q$ the function
$t\mapsto\dim_{\kappa(t)}H^q(X_t,\cF_t)$ is upper semicontinuous on
$T$, and there are canonical base-change maps
$R^qf_*\cF\otimes\kappa(t)\to H^q(X_t,\cF_t)$. If moreover $T$ is
*reduced* and this function is locally constant, then $R^qf_*\cF$ is
finite locally free (in particular flat) and the base-change maps in
degree $q$ are isomorphisms.

proof.text: Fix an integer $q$. Apply [thm-pc-semicontinuity-base-change] to the given $f:X\to T$, $\mathcal F=\cF$, and this $q$: its hypotheses are exactly that $f$ is proper of finite presentation and $\cF$ is of finite presentation and flat over $T$. Its fibre $X_t=X\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ and pulled-back sheaf $\mathcal F_t$ are the fibres in the present statement. Clause (1) supplies the canonical maps $\varphi^q(t):R^qf_*\cF\otimes_{\mathcal O_T}\kappa(t)\to H^q(X_t,\cF_t)$ for every $t$.

Clause (2) of [thm-pc-semicontinuity-base-change] states that $\beta^q(t)=\dim_{\kappa(t)}H^q(X_t,\cF_t)$ is upper semicontinuous on $T$. This is exactly the function in the item, so it proves the asserted semicontinuity.

Now suppose $T$ is reduced and the displayed fibre-dimension function is locally constant. These are precisely the additional hypotheses of clause (3) of [thm-pc-semicontinuity-base-change]. That clause gives $R^qf_*\cF$ finite locally free, in particular flat, and states that the same canonical $\varphi^q(t)$ from clause (1) is an isomorphism at every $t$. The choice of integer $q$ was arbitrary, proving all the assertions without a Noetherian hypothesis or a constant-rank hypothesis across different connected components.
